This matter is taken up through Hybrid mode.
2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for the State-Opposite Party.
Perused the materials placed before this Court.

3. The present bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail relating to Berhampur Cyber P.S. Case No.13 of 2024, corresponding to G.R. Case No.772 of 2024, pending before the learned S.D.J.M., Berhampur, for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 420 & 34 of IPC.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that earlier this matter was not before any other Bench of this Court.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner is in custody since 03.06.2024.
He further contended that the investigation has been completed and the final charge-sheet has been filed in the meantime.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner further contended that one Rahul Kumar Jena is the principal accused, who happens to be the son of the present Petitioner.

She further referring to the impugned rejection order, contended that a sum of Rs.15,66,057/- has been transferred to the account of Amit Kumar Das out of a total misappropriated sum of Rs.23,03,668/-.

She further contended that the sole basis of implication of the present Petitioner is the CCTV footage wherein the Petitioner has been seen to have been withdrawing money from the Canara Bank account belonging to M/s. Tirupati South Indian Pradip Kumar Jena vs State Of Odisha .....

sentences.text:
Opposite Parties on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72850149/
1 Restaurant and Anil Kumar Das.
The ATM Card of Anil Kumar Das was also recovered from the possession of the present Petitioner.

Further, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner does not have any criminal antecedent and that since the Petitioner belongs to locality, there is no chance of absconding.
It was also contended that the principal accused Rahul Kumar Jena has passed away in the meantime on 24.02.2024.

In such view of the matter, learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner be released on bail on any terms and condition deemed fit by this Court which the Petitioner undertakes to abide by while on bail.
5. Learned counsel for the State on the other hand objected to release of the Petitioner on bail on the ground that the allegations made in the FIR are grave and serious in nature.
He further submitted that in the event, the Petitioner is released on bail, it will difficult to recover the money belonging to the complainant.
Therefore, he submitted that the prayer for bail of the Petitioner be rejected at this juncture.

6. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the respective parties and on a careful consideration of the surrounding facts as well as materials on record, and the fact that the charge-sheet has already been filed, and the fact that the Petitioner does not have any similar criminal antecedents, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.40,000/- (Rupees Forty Thousand) with two solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned court in seisin over the matter.
Violation of any of the terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.

7. It is further directed that the bail granted to the Petitioner is subject to depositing a cash security of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) before the learned Court in seisin over the matter,
which shall be kept in any Nationalized Bank in interest bearing account initially for a period of one year which will be renewable from time to time till conclusion of trial and the same shall be abide by the final outcome of the trial of the case.
In addition to that the Petitioner shall also furnish a property security to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs).
8. It is further directed that the bail granted to the Petitioner is subject to the condition that the court below shall verify whether the Petitioner is having any similar criminal antecedent.
In the event it is found that the Petitioner is having any similar criminal antecedent, this bail order shall automatically stand revoked.
Violation of any of the terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
9. The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.
( A.K. Mohapatra) Judge S.K. Rout Signature Not Verified Digitally Signed Signed by: SANTANU KUMAR ROUT Reason: Authentication
